title: perf-canary/telemetry: add per-model metrics aggregation + normalization helper
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Motivation: perf-canary and the Grafana dashboard queries need a consistent definition of per-model metrics across services (canary runner, runtime telemetry pipeline, and alert evaluation). We currently have multiple slightly-different implementations of: unit conversions (ms vs s), histogram bucket alignment, label normalization (model vs model_id vs model_version), and derived signals (tokens/sec from token_count + duration). These differences are causing alert/query mismatches and make regression triage slower. This PR introduces a shared helper for per-model aggregation + normalization, intended to be used by perf-canary (PR-19218) and by the metrics pipeline/queries feeding dashboards/alerts. Summary of changes: (1) Add PerModelNormalizer + helpers to produce canonical metric names, units, and histogram buckets; (2) Add derived metric builders (e2e_latency_ms, runtime_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec) with consistent math and guardrails; (3) Introduce a small label sanitizer to enforce the agreed label set (model, model_version, region, hardware_sku, runtime_build, kernel_id) and drop high-cardinality/unapproved labels; (4) Provide a compatibility shim for existing metric names so dashboards don’t break during rollout; (5) Add unit tests with golden bucket boundaries + sample inputs from perf-canary staging runs. Behavior details: - Latency units: canonical is milliseconds (ms). Any inputs in seconds are converted to ms at ingest. - Histograms: canonical buckets (ms) are [5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300, 500, 750, 1000, 1500, 2000, 3000, 5000, 10000] with a separate tighter set for runtime-only latency. The helper exports both and chooses based on metric kind. - tokens/sec: computed as (output_tokens / decode_wall_time_seconds). If decode_wall_time is missing, fallback to (output_tokens / total_wall_time_seconds) but emits a counter indicating fallback path for visibility. - Model identifiers: canonicalizes to model=<registry_name> and model_version=<semver-ish or digest> where available; if only a legacy model_id exists, maps through the registry resolver interface (pluggable) and emits a warning-level log once per process (rate-limited) when mapping fails. - Label policy: drops request_id, tenant_id, route, and prompt_shape from emitted metrics by default (they can still exist in logs/traces), to avoid cardinality blowups. Testing: - Unit tests cover unit conversion, histogram bucket selection, derived tokens/sec math, and label filtering. - Added a small fuzz-ish test around label sanitizer to ensure we don’t accidentally permit new labels without an allowlist update. Rollout plan: - Land helper behind an internal package path and adopt it in perf-canary next. - Keep compatibility names for 2 weeks while dashboards migrate; after that we can remove the old names and update the alerts in observability-pack. Checklist: [x] Backward compatible metric names for existing dashboards; [x] Cardinality review: only allowlisted labels; [x] Added tests and golden buckets; [x] Added docs in code comments for canonical metric contract. Notes: This does not change runtime emission yet; it only standardizes aggregation/normalization on the consumer side. A follow-up will migrate the runtime exporter to use the same bucket boundaries for end-to-end consistency.
commits: telemetry: add per-model normalizer and canonical metric contract
telemetry: derived metrics for tokens/sec and latency breakdowns
telemetry: histogram bucket sets + golden tests
docs/tests: add usage examples and update package comments
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we be explicit about the canonical unit in the helper API? I don’t want downstream folks passing seconds into something named *_ms.

Caleb Johnson (author): Good call. Updated the public helpers to accept time.Duration and renamed the float-based entrypoints to *FromSeconds/*FromMillis to force clarity. Also added package-level comment: canonical output is ms.
Nadia Rahman (review): Histogram buckets: do we have a rationale for the bucket cutoffs? Also, we should ensure the canary and dashboards use the same buckets or queries get weird.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added a docstring explaining buckets are tuned for our typical p95 ranges and alert thresholds. Also split into E2E vs runtime-only bucket sets with explicit exported constants so dashboards can reference the same list.
Allison Grant (review): Please ensure label sanitizer drops route + request_id. I’m worried about cardinality after the alert storm incident.
Caleb Johnson (author): Yup—route/request_id/tenant_id are hard-denied. Added a fuzz-ish test to ensure new labels don’t slip through without updating the allowlist.
Omar El-Sayed (review): tokens/sec formula: can we surface whether we used decode time vs total time? That’s important for attribution.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added a counter metric permodel_tokens_per_sec_fallback_total{reason=missing_decode_time} and exposed it via the helper so canary can alert when we’re falling back too much.
Logan Wright (review): Looks good. One nit: compat names should be time-limited; add a TODO with an owner/date.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added TODO referencing ENG-4882 and a 2-week cleanup note in the package comment.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Thanks for baking in the label policy + tests.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved. Please coordinate adoption with perf-canary PR-19218 so we don’t fork behavior again.
release_notes: Internal: Introduces shared per-model metrics normalization helper (units, histogram buckets, derived tokens/sec) to keep perf-canary, dashboards, and alerts consistent.
